MINUTES
  MALIBU PLANNING COMMISSION
  REGULAR MEETING
  NOVEMBER 21, 2022
  TELECONFERENCED VARIOUS LOCATIONS
  -

  6:30 P.M.

The following meeting was held pursuant to the Governor’s Executive Orders N-25-20 and N-29-
20 and fully teleconferenced from various locations during the coronavirus disease (COVID- 19)
pandemic.

CALL TO ORDER

  Chair Smith called the meeting to order at 7:02 p.m. due to a technical issue with
  LiveStream. Staff posted a message that directed the public to the virtual meeting link and
  informed them that video of the meeting would be made available online the following
  day.

ROLL CALL

  The following persons were recorded in attendance by the Recording Secretary:

  PRESENT: Chair Dennis R. Smith, Vice Chair John Mazza and Commissioners Kraig Hill,
  Jeffrey Jennings and Mark Wetton

  ALSO PRESENT: Patrick Donegan, Assistant City Attorney; Richard Mollica, Planning
  Director; Adrian Fernandez, Assistant Planning Director; Troy Spayd, Assistant Public
  Works Director; Patricia Salazar, Development and Operations Manager; Jessica
  Thompson, Senior Planner; Adam Pisarkiewicz, Contract Planner; Lauren Doyel, Contract
  Coastal Engineer and Geotechnical Reviewer; and Rebecca Evans, Recording Secretary

APPROVAL OF AGENDA

MOTION  Vice Chair Mazza moved and Commissioner Wetton seconded a motion to approve
  the agenda as recommended by staff and to continue Item No. 5.C. to a date
  uncertain and to continue Item No. 5.D. to the December 5, 2022 Regular Planning
  Commission meeting.

  The question was called and the motion carried unanimously.

REPORT ON POSTING OF AGENDA

  Recording Secretary Evans reported that the agenda for the meeting was properly posted
  on November 10, 2022.

ITEM 1  CEREMONIAL/PRESENTATIONS
  None.

ITEM 2.A.  PUBLIC COMMENTS

  Norm Haynie questioned if Planning had recently used new interpretations of long-
  existing development definitions and cited a recent interpretation of Local
  Implementation Plan Section 6.5(B)(4).

  Ryan Embree expressed concern that the antenna tower at 23555 West Civic Center
  Way was a changed use from the original project, which included a building that
  housed the radio equipment enclosed with brick to match the sheriffs station. The
  current tower did not incorporate into the Santa Monica Community College and
  was intended for commercial use rather than the emergency use described in the
  original application.

ITEM 2.B.  COMMISSION / STAFF COMMENTS

  Vice Chair Mazza stated Planning staff should maintain and make a current
  interpretations manual readily available to the public to ensure all applicants were
  treated equally. He asked for clarification on Mr. Embree’s comments and
  questioned if a project postcard he recently received with an image of the whole
  county building was related to the wireless tower.

  In response to Vice Chair Mazza, Planning Director Mollica stated Los Angeles
  County was asked to apply for an amendment for the antenna tower height and
  provide a current survey of the height. The City was waiting for the County to
  proceed, and any proposed amendment or conditional use permit would be brought
  to the Planning Commission. The postcard recently received by Vice Chair Mazza
  related to a separate item.

  Commissioner Hill questioned whether there should have been a public hearing
  notice for the fully screened rooftop equipment on the Los Angeles County
  building, rather than treatment as an administrative issue.

  In response to Commissioner Hill, Planning Director Mollica clarified that the item
  was submitted for an Administrative Plan Review and if found to meet defined
  criteria, a decision would be rendered by the Planning Director. If the discretionary
  request for height was determined to be consistent with the Site Plan Review criteria
  found in Chapter 17, it would also be within the Planning Director’s purview to
  approve. The item would then be appealable to the Planning Commission due to
  the Site Plan Review. However, the Malibu Municipal Code provided no
  mechanism for the Planning Director to forward the issue to the Planning
  Commission. Assistant City Attorney Donegan confirmed the Planning Director’s
   Malibu Planning Commission
  Minutes of November 21, 2022
  Page 3 of 10

  clarification of the Malibu Municipal Code.

  Commissioner Hill suggested the addition of a public information option for
  administrative actions with a high level of public interest. Planning Director
  Mollica offered to forward the sections of the Malibu Municipal Code that apply to
  decisions of the Planning Director and reviewing authority.

  Vice Chair Mazza suggested the item should be treated as a public works project,
  and therefore handled differently.

  In response to Vice Chair Mazza, Assistant City Attorney Donegan stated the
  Administrative Plan Review was appropriate for the item.

  Commissioner Wetton asked if any Administrative Plan Review could be appealed
  to the Planning Commission.

  In response to Commissioner Wetton, Planning Director Mollica stated if there was
  a discretionary item attached to an Administrative Plan Review, the proposed
  development could go to the Planning Commission upon appeal and could be
  further appealed to the City Council.

  Commissioner Jennings stated years ago the Planning Commission had a dispute
  over whether the Planning Director on his own could negatively determine that an
  Administrative Plan Review was not appropriate, and that decision was not
  appealable. However, a positive decision by the Planning Director would not come
  to the Planning Commission without an appeal.

  Chair Smith expressed concern regarding the 24-hour rule for responses to
  members of the public and questioned if Planning Department staff might need
  additional time to respond rather than upset members of the public who don’t
  receive a response within 24 hours.

  Planning Director Mollica agreed that perhaps a longer timeframe was needed until
  staffing issues were resolved.
